### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **107** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via action_button (literal, a string literal in testButton))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `04636fca74e249c145b19d8af897e06ccc92d1f6` — the merge of head `289f3e093737910e32b610f060d166ae9ba6c629` into base `c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 04636fca74e249c145b19d8af897e06ccc92d1f6 && git checkout 04636fca74e249c145b19d8af897e06ccc92d1f6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47 289f3e093737910e32b610f060d166ae9ba6c629 && git checkout -B drift-repro c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47 && git merge --no-ff 289f3e093737910e32b610f060d166ae9ba6c629

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c2bfa3ef7c24c98434538d4406cc46f90c1d8e47` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `289f3e093737910e32b610f060d166ae9ba6c629`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of the `ai` settings namespace widens: new keys `default_model`, `<provider>_enabled` (9), `<provider>_models` (9), `structured_output_provider`, `structured_output_model`; new actions `test_<provider>` (9). Right: each is additive, `provider` keeps its key and stored values (now "default provider"), and no existing key changes meaning for a stored value set.
- New save refusal (`SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `invalid_value`, `constraint.rule` from five named rules) applies only when a new key is set inconsistently; a legacy value set (only `provider` + `<provider>_model`) trips none of them (`aiModelRuleBreaches` reads `default_model` / `structured_output_*` blank ⇒ no breach). Right.
- New package exports (`AI_PROVIDERS`, `resolveAiModelConfiguration`, `aiModelRuleBreaches`, `parseAiModelList`, `registerAiModelRules` + types) are additive public surface of `@objectstack/service-settings`. Right.
- Hosted projection (`cloud-managed-settings.ts`) hides every new key and refuses every new action, so hosted tenants gain no new surface. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-settings` minor for additive keys/exports — matches. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` agree with the diff (authorable keys added to a published manifest).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag: overlap with objectstack-ai/objectstack#37668 on the corpus count line only; second to land sets it. Accepted as a landing note.
- `resolveAiModelConfiguration` folds an unset structured-output choice into the default provider's first model. The cloud consumer (objectstack-ai/cloud#5060) must keep today's env/pinned structured-output model when the admin set none, so it has to read the raw `structured_output_model` / `structured_output_provider` blank state, not only the resolved choice. Carried to that card's order (N1 below).
- SQL push-down: not applicable (no data access).
- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` via the relay.

### ④ Design judgment

Not owed on the declaration face. Read anyway: the visibility predicate `on(provider)` (default provider or its toggle) matches `isAiProviderEnabled`; keys stay one encrypted `password` field per provider; only existing specifier kinds are used (`toggle`, `textarea` with `pattern`, `text`, `action_button`), no spec change.

- N1 (nit) — structured-output "unset" is not distinguishable in `AiModelConfiguration`; consumer reads raw values (see ③).

No must-fix, no should-fix.
